key_insight: PIF-MIONet combines interacting input-function encoders with physics-informed learning to predict fluid flow within an FEM-coupled poroelasticity framework.
engineering_relevance: The framework targets costly coupled poroelasticity simulations while retaining FEM for mechanical equilibrium and enabling integration with the open-source GEOS simulator.
method: Stagger FEM mechanical-equilibrium solves with neural fluid-flow predictions through IFENN.
Fuse MIONet branch outputs to enable early interaction among input functions.
Combine physics and data losses, with domain decomposition for complex geometries and localized flow.
evidence_signal: Tests cover 2D and 3D domains, variable material properties and time discretizations, and unseen loading histories; for complex cases, physics-plus-data training used only 0.1% of the training increments used in purely data-driven training.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify end-to-end speedup or establish industrial-scale performance; the reported training-increment reduction is not a runtime reduction.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet with IFENN: A Generalized Framework for Coupled Poroelasticity Problems
